children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a rectangle whose area is a reasonable approximation of the area of South Australia.

answer.short: A rectangle approximating South Australia, balancing the areas included outside the state against the areas omitted inside it.
answer.worked: Draw the rectangle over the South Australia region of the map. Choose its boundaries so that the areas included outside the state approximately balance the areas of the state left outside the rectangle.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Measure its side lengths, and hence calculate the approximate area of the state.

answer.short: Answers depend on the rectangle drawn. At the map scale, if its measured sides are $l$ mm and $w$ mm, the approximate area is $784lw\text{ km}^2$.
answer.worked:
The map scale is $1:28\,000\,000$.
$$\begin{align*}1\text{ mm on the map}&=28\,000\,000\text{ mm in reality}\\1\text{ mm on the map}&=28\text{ km in reality}\end{align*}$$
For rectangle sides measuring $l$ mm and $w$ mm:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Actual length}&=28l\text{ km}\\\text{Actual width}&=28w\text{ km}\\\text{Approximate area}&=(28l)(28w)\text{ km}^2\\\text{Approximate area}&=784lw\text{ km}^2\end{align*}$$
